headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: broad-network content writer paired with writable, browser-enabled document processor can exfiltrate or overwrite shared work by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has broad network egress and is a content-writing agent; B can read files, run browsers, and parse stdin/stdout. If A’s outputs are fed into B through files or pipes, B may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The shared bridge is plausible from the profiles, but not directly documented, so uncertainty stays medium.
conditions: IF A's generated text is passed into B via files or stdin/stdout
IF B uses file or stream content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance header to A outputs
Require B to ignore imperative text in inputs
Insert a manual review step before B acts on A output
Use separate temp directories for handoff
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-detection filters

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches text, audio, images, video, and multimodal data and has broad network egress; A also has broad network egress. If they share a workspace, B can read local files and transmit their contents, creating a realistic leakage path. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem or workspace
IF sensitive files are placed in that shared workspace
mitigations: Keep agents in separate directories
Restrict B's read access to a staging folder
Disable network egress for B during review
Move sensitive inputs out of shared paths
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent sandboxing and egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B can write the filesystem, execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and install packages; A is a content-writing agent with broad network egress. If both operate on the same directory, B’s writes can overwrite or race with A’s generated artifacts, and B supports multiple instances, increasing collision risk. The shared mutable target is not explicit, so uncertainty is resolved upward.
conditions: IF A and B write to the same directory
IF B runs multiple instances against shared mutable files
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Make A outputs read-only before B consumes them
Serialize B instances on shared resources
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce content that B may ingest through files or stdin/stdout, and B has browser and shell execution plus broad network egress. That creates a pathway where A’s output becomes B’s operational input without a verification gate. The profiles do not show explicit automation from A to B, so medium is the appropriate default.
conditions: IF B consumes A's output as authoritative input
IF B performs actions based on that input without verification
mitigations: Require a human check before B acts
Add schema validation to A outputs
Have B cite source evidence before acting
Limit B to read-only mode for first pass
requires-engineering: implement verification and approval workflow

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source content-writing/listing agent with no data classes touched, while B processes text, audio, images, video, and multimodal data. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a small compliance gap is plausible if regulated data is introduced into B. A is cited for its minimal data footprint; B is cited for the broader compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed into B
IF B's API or retention policy differs from the operator's compliance requirements
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to B
Tag sensitive inputs before processing
Review B's retention settings
Keep compliance-sensitive workloads on a separate path
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
